381	The first example, the first thing, was in Egypt.
382	We see that Yaakov Avinu went down to Egypt.
383	He went down with all seventy souls, and he established there
384	synagogues and study halls and commanded everyone to learn.
385	And everyone sat and learned and was connected to the Torah,
386	connected to holiness, kept their holiness,
387	and took a different city from all of Egypt. All of Egypt
388	was on one side, and they took a city
389	set apart from Egypt so as not to mix with them. They took
390	the land of Goshen, which was a bit far from Egypt, from all
391	their settlements.
392	And indeed they succeeded. As long as Yaakov Avinu
393	was alive, and the tribes, the whole Jewish people was connected
394	to the Torah, connected to the mitzvot, there were no problems.
395	But after Yaakov Avinu passed away, and after
396	a few years the tribes also passed away, "and Yosef died,
397	and all his brothers, and all that generation," and "a new king
398	arose who did not know Yosef."
399	On the face of it, what happened here?
400	After Yosef passed away and all the tribes passed away,
401	the Jewish people began to scatter, began to go
402	and mingle with the nations, began to go to their circuses,
403	to their places of entertainment, and suddenly the nations
404	saw, the Egyptians saw a circus

406	bothered them, little by little,
407	until they began to intermarry with them.
408	Then came the harsh blow of the Egyptian bondage, with all those
409	troubles. The Midrashim tell of troubles
410	beyond comprehension that were there: they would put children
411	into the walls in place of bricks,
412	they would beat them without mercy. Pharaoh,
413	wicked Pharaoh, would slaughter 150 children every day
414	in the morning and 150 children in the evening, to bathe in their blood.
415	That is what they told his magicians. Things the ear
416	cannot bear to hear, for whoever looks a little into the Midrashim.
417	Terribly, terribly frightening things.

419	returned to their place, then we see that no one
420	could touch them. They defeated Sichon

423	connected to the Torah.
